title: Per-tenant SCIM Reconciliation and Multi-org Access Certification Pipeline
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers require an auditable, per-tenant certification workflow that reconciles SCIM source-of-truth with our RBAC provisioning and generates time-bound evidence bundles for regulators. Current exports are coarse-grained and require manual stitching for multi-org customers, leading to slow quarterly reviews and missed attestations.

Goal: Build a pipeline that performs continuous SCIM reconciliation per tenant, surfaces drift (active accounts not in SCIM, SCIM accounts without access, role mismatches), automates periodic certification emails with escalation, and emits signed evidence bundles (JSON + SHA256 + signing metadata) consumable by GRC vendors. The pipeline must be privacy- and residency-aware (tenant-scoped residency settings) and allow opt-in for external GRC integration (OneTrust/Drata-style webhooks).

Scope:
- Per-tenant SCIM delta processor with configurable cadence (realtime for high-sensitivity tenants, daily for others).
- Role-to-permission mapping verification and drift classification (assignment mismatch, stale service accounts, orphaned permissions).
- Certification flow orchestration: scheduled reviewer assignment, reminders, automated escalation, and final attestation capture.
- Evidence packaging: tamper-evident signed export, retention metadata, tenant residency tag, and export-level redaction rules.
- Integrations: optional webhook to customer GRC, and a Redwood Console page for reviewers to complete remediation tasks.

Non-goals: Providing a full-featured GRC product; replacing SSO provider. We will not change SCIM schemas or force provider upgrades as part of this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant reconciliation runs and produces a drift report (CSV + structured JSON) for >95% of tenants with SCIM enabled
Certification job can be scheduled per-tenant with configurable cadence and reviewer list
Evidence bundle includes: reconciliation summary, list of attestations, SHA256 checksum, signing metadata, tenant residency tag, and a retention flag
Console reviewer workflow shows drift items and allows 'Remediate', 'Acknowledge', or 'Escalate' with comments
Webhook consumer can fetch evidence bundle via signed URL valid for configurable TTL
Automated reminders and escalation rules trigger on schedule and create remediation tickets when required
tasks: Design SCIM delta model and storage schema (per-tenant partitions)
Implement reconciliation worker with pluggable cadence and backoff
Create drift classification logic and severity mapping
Implement evidence bundler and signing (KMS integration) with residency metadata
Expose reviewer UI in Console with action buttons and audit trail
Add webhook delivery and retry semantics for GRC partners
Create a small migration job for tenants using bulk exports to bootstrap state
Add e2e tests and unit tests for reconciliation, signing, and retention enforcement
Document the API and reviewer workflow for support and sales
notes: Design decision: store reconciliation snapshots in tenant-scoped S3 prefixes (or equivalent) tagged with region/residency to satisfy data residency requests
We will use existing KMS/HSM integration for signing evidence bundles; need key access policy for the reconciliation service account
To support high-sensitivity customers, add a realtime webhook mode that streams SCIM deltas rather than relying on periodic pulls
Retention enforcement will use a separate scheduler job to mark and delete evidence per tenant retention settings using legal hold exemptions where present

risks: High-churn tenants may produce large reconciliation payloads and S3 cost; will need rate-limiting and sampling for audit exports
Signing keys must be tightly controlled; losing a key requires re-signing evidence which is expensive
Incorrect drift classification could cause noise and reviewer fatigue; include sampling + human-in-the-loop for first 30 days after rollout
Data residency enforcement must be validated end-to-end; mistakes could trigger compliance incidents
